summary:
HMS-of-A (Health Monitoring System of Astronauts) is an offline-first, multimodal biometric and clinical triage platform developed by Team Linkbeing for long-duration spaceflight. 

The system integrates 20 health and environmental metrics across seven domains - combining smartwatch telemetry, microfluidic sweat assays, EEG, cabin ECLSS sensors, and contactless edge AI. Using local computer vision and voice biomarker analysis, it monitors fatigue, pulse, and vocal stress directly on-station.
details:
To address the lack of cohesive orbital health tools, HMS-of-A utilizes a three-layer AI engine - combining clinical thresholds, norm-gated personalized baselines, and a denoising autoencoder - to distinguish normal EVA workload from hazardous physiological drift. Dual-role Commander and Crew portals streamline diagnostics with guided zero-G medical procedures, 18 emergency playbooks, and gamified checkup streaks.

By processing raw video and audio strictly in volatile RAM and transmitting only lightweight scalar metrics, the system protects crew privacy and operates independently of Earth-link latency. Ultimately, it safeguards astronaut readiness against radiation, microgravity, and isolation, with direct applications for extreme terrestrial environments like polar expeditions and aviation.
